notes: 1 FAS 0210 is a non-degree, credit-bearing course that is required for graduation. It provides 2 non-degree credits, which do not count toward your degree requirements.

2 All degree-seeking students must complete 2 SCH in Arabic by enrolling in one designated course. Placement is determined as follows: → Students holding a Moroccan baccalaureate are automatically enrolled in ARB 1241 without a placement test. → Students holding a cultural mission baccalaureate (French, Spanish, among others) must take a placement test to determine their appropriate one ARB course. → Students holding an international high school diploma with no prior Arabic instruction must take a placement test to determine their appropriate one ARA course.

3 Students with a Moroccan baccalaureate must complete 2 SCH in French by taking FRN 3210 as their exit -level course. All newly admitted students must take the free international Test d’Évaluation de Français (TEF) to determine their required French courses and levels. If TEF results indicate additional prerequisite courses, these will not count toward the degree. Students cannot take French in their first semester and may be exempted with a minimum C1 in TEF and 16 in GAT. International students with no prior French knowledge may fulfill their GenEd language requirement with Spanish, German, Turkish, Italian, or Korean.

4 Students minoring in Business Administration must take MTH 1305 as part of their GenEd requirements. If they take MTH 1388 as a prerequisite for MTH 1305, its credits will not count toward the degree.

5 A course with an SL component must be taken as co-requisites. Failing the course will de facto result in failing the SL component, too. Failing the SL component will result in an NRP in the SL component only. Students who fail the SL component must enroll in another course from their degree plan with an SL component in the subsequent semesters.
6 In case no subsequent course in the student’s degree plan is offered with an SL component, he/she must submit an SL proposal to the SLP Committee and enroll in SLP 1101.
